newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua prepares for historic handover of power.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua prepares for historic handover of power.

text.p: Seven Latin American presidents and delegations from 40 countries will attend the January 10 inauguration of Arnoldo Aleman as the new president of Nicaragua, a Foreign Ministry spokeswoman said on Monday.

At the ceremony, President Violeta Chamorro will pass on the presidential sash to Aleman, the right-wing president-elect, who defeated left-wing Sandinista candidate Daniel Ortega in Nicaragua's October 20 elections.
It will mark the first time in more than 100 years of Nicaraguan history that one democratically-elected, civilian president handed over power to another.

Confirmed to attend are Paraguayan President Juan Carlos Wasmosy, Dominican Republic President Leonel Fernandez, Costa Rican President Jose Maria Figueres, El Salvadorean President Armando Calderon Sol, Guatemalan President Alvaro Arzu, Panamanian President Ernesto Perez Balladares and Honduran President Carlos Roberto Reina, Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Claudia Paniagua said.
Nicaraguan police have said more than 700 police officers and firefighters will provide security for the event, which will be held in Managua's 20,000-seat National Stadium.
